sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Republic of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1985, as amended)
Luxembourg–Netherlands Tax Agreement applicable through the Benelux framework
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (pending ratification, not directly invoked at Stage 1)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the RBE; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of UBO's country of residence (e.g., passport issuance authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country is a party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each UBO (utility bill, bank statement or officially attested equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank or competent municipal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for non-Luxembourg documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation, signed by all founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (for domestic execution) or apostilled/consularized foreign notary (for foreign execution)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and copy of constitutive documents of any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies of the foreign shareholder's country (e.g., UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of subscription and payment of share capital (blocked on a Luxembourg bank account pending incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution or ELTI (Établissement de crédit) or bank branch in Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required (domestic issuance); authenticated by the issuing bank's stamp and signature

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and shareholders against the Luxembourg consolidated financial sanctions list (Ministry of Finance), UN Security Council sanctions, EU restrictive measures (OJ L series), OFAC SDN list and other applicable regimes; automated real-time screening through a licensed commercial AML database; PEP status checked for potential high-risk designation; enhanced due diligence where any PEP, sanctions hit or negative news is identified; screening results documented and retained for at least 5 years after termination of business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be drafted in Latin script; French, German and Luxembourgish are accepted; the name must be consistent with Luxembourg naming conventions and clearly distinguishable from existing names; foreign-language names may be accepted if transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a French or German translation of any legal form requirements; the corporate form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a name reservation, the applicant receives a formal refusal notification via the LBR portal. The applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days of the refusal, setting out the grounds for distinguishability and compliance; the appeal is reviewed by the RCS authority and, if rejected, a further judicial appeal may be lodged with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Chambre commerciale). A new name reservation can also be filed immediately, with payment of a fresh fee. Extension of a valid name reservation is not automatic; after expiry the name is released and must be re-reserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted – a physical registered office in Luxembourg is mandatory for a SARL; a pure virtual office (shared address without a physical presence) is not accepted by the RCS and would undermine the economic substance requirement for financial portfolio tracking activities; a law firm or fiduciary office in Luxembourg may serve as the registered office if it includes an actual physical location and people with administrative authority, but this is not considered a virtual office for AML purposes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation fee at LBR/RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for name reservation and preliminary search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of Articles of Association (statuts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of the Chamber of Notaries for a SARL incorporation with standard clauses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) registration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule for electronic registration of a SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation excerpt in the Official Gazette (RESA – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
Hague Apostille and certified translation of foreign UBO and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign apostille authorities and certified Luxembourg translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rates for apostille issue (state fee) and sworn translation per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT, PEP and sanctions screening of UBOs and directors (pre-incorporation compliance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider or law firm conducting due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for statutory UBO identification, PIPS/RBE checks, and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, particularly SARL Articles 180-1 to 180-29 (modernised by the Law of 23 December 2016 on the reform of the SARL), together with Articles 40-58 on general company formation; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (Loi du 19 décembre 2002 concernant le registre de commerce et des sociétés), Articles 9, 18 and 19; Grand-Ducal Regulation on RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 250 Route d'Esch, L-1471 Luxembourg; electronic portal: https://www.lbr.lu; filings are transmitted by the notary through LBR's e-filing service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif / Statuts) authenticated by a Luxembourg notary, followed by the formal RCS registration filing (Demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) and legal publication of an excerpt in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Following the Law of 23 December 2016, the minimum share capital of a SARL is EUR 1, fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash before execution of the notarial deed. Luxembourg law imposes no mandatory escrow account; however, notarial practice requires a banker's certificate evidencing that the full capital has been irrevocably credited to the SARL's account. Contributions in kind are permitted but require a report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) and full transfer of the asset at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By unanimous consent of the subscribers, the below resolution is adopted as the First Board Resolution of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée in formation. 1. Subscription of share capital: the shares are deemed fully subscribed and paid-up in cash as reflected by the banker's certificate. 2. Registered office: the Company's registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, with immediate effect. 3. Articles: the Articles of Association as initialed are adopted in full. 4. Officer appointments: [Gérant name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant), with full power to represent the Company, and [alternate name] is appointed alternate. 5. Filings: the Manager is authorised to complete RCS, RESA, VAT, corporate tax, UBO and social security filings. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and certificate of non-use
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Name Registration Office, 250 Route d'Esch, L-1471 Luxembourg; online name search at https://www.lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written or e-portal request for a Certificat de non-usage listing two proposed corporate names in descending priority. The RCS verifies the names against the trade register and the company-name database. Upon clearance, obtain the certificate of non-use and deliver it to the notary before signing the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed name-reservation request form (LBR name clearance form)
Two alternative proposed corporate names ending with 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL'
Copy of each subscriber's national ID card or passport
Notarized power of attorney, if the request is filed by a representative
Completed non-use certificate questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first-choice name conflicts with an existing registered company or protected trade name, immediately switch to the second alternative name or file a fresh request with a distinct memorandum; the certificate is preliminary, so no adverse registration record accrues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate bank account and payment of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution chosen by the founders (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Raiffeisen, Spuerkees) or an authorized fintech/EMI; the banker's certificate must be addressed to the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the SARL in formation, deposit the fully subscribed cash capital (minimum EUR 1), and obtain a banker's certificate (attestation de blocage / de crédit des fonds) confirming the funds are irrevocably credited to the company's account. Deliver the banker's certificate to the notary for attachment to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Subscription list (liste des souscripteurs) with share allocation
KYC/AML documentation for each shareholder: passport, proof of address, source of funds and source of wealth
Description of the commercial activity (ISIC 6201 software and cloud portfolio tracking)
Bank account-opening forms and mandate
Draft Articles of Association for the bank's client documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence or refuses the file, supplement with an organizational chart, detailed source-of-wealth declaration and the software business plan; alternatively select another licensed credit institution and re-initiate the account opening while the notarial drafting continues in parallel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation (Acte constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed by the founders and admitted to the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg; only Luxembourg notaries may authenticate the Articles of Association.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Articles of Association using the cleared name and corporate purpose covering software development, cloud computing, financial portfolio analytics and related ICT services. The subscribers (or their attorney-in-fact) appear before the notary and execute the authentic deed. The deed must state the corporate name, registered office, duration, object, share capital, number of shares and par value, contribution details, number of managers and the signing manager's acceptance of office. The notary verifies the banker's certificate and all legal formalities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of non-usage for the corporate name
Banker's certificate evidencing full payment of the share capital
Approved final text of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
Identity documents or attestations of identity of each subscriber and each manager
Report of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé), if any in-kind contribution is made
Signed declaration of acceptance of office by the appointed Manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues drafting queries, incorporate the requisitions and re-sign the deed; if a subscriber withdraws, substitute the subscriber and re-execute; the deed may be re-notarized with a supplementary preparatory act before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Corporate Registration Department, via notarial e-filing and the LBR electronic platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory one-month period following the notarial deed, the notary transmits the authenticated deed and the registration request to the RCS. The RCS verifies the file, allocates a permanent RCS registration number, records the company in the national trade register and arranges publication of a legal excerpt in the RESA. The issuance of the RCS extract marks the completion of incorporation and renders the company opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: Original notarial minute of the deed of incorporation
Registration request (demande d'inscription) signed by the notary or appointed representative
Copy of the certificate of non-usage
Manager appointment and acceptance clauses contained in the deed
RCS statistical annex declaring the NACE/ISIC 6201 activity code
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (régularisation) for a missing or defective exhibit, the notary files the corrective document within the granted grace period; if the deed contains inconsistencies, file a formal request for rectification with the RCS; legal personality is confirmed upon the RCS certificate of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and national business number registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for the national business number and Luxembourg VAT; Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — bureau d'imposition for corporate income tax; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for employer registration, if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the AEDT allocates the 13-digit national business number to the company. The company must file the VAT registration application (Form 011 — déclaration d'assujettissement) since its cloud subscription and license revenues are taxable supplies in Luxembourg (standard rate 17%, reduced rates 8% and 3% for eligible categories). Open the corporate income tax file with the ACD by submitting the registered-office and business-purpose details and file the first corporate income tax return in accordance with the tax year. If employees are engaged, register as an employer with the CCSS.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (extrait du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
Manager identification documents
VAT registration form (Form 011) with declared activity and expected turnover
Corporate income tax registration notice addressed to the ACD bureau d'imposition
Minutes appointing the Manager and details of the signatory rights
Bank details (IBAN) of the SARL's account
CCSS employer registration form (only if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the 13-digit number or VAT attestation is delayed beyond the SLA, apply ex officio through the AEDT regional bureau with a copy of the RCS extract; late VAT registration is regularized by voluntary declaration, and the AEDT allocates the number retroactively to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership designation, substance and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Commune of the registered office for fire-safety and occupancy clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month from RCS registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) in the RBE, identifying each ultimate beneficial owner with a shareholding or control exceeding 25% and the precise nature and extent of the interest. Obtain the occupational fire-safety and office occupancy clearance from the local Commune, and file the first-hire/worksite declaration with the ITM before employees commence work. Maintain statutory corporate records, minutes and share register at the registered office in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: RBE filing form with complete UBO details and supporting passport copies
RCS extract evidencing the incorporation
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of the registered office
Commune fire-safety clearance application including floor plans and premises capacity
ITM first-hire or workplace declaration (if employees will be engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE rejects a declaration, correct and re-submit within the same statutory 30-day window and respond to any LBR information demand; if the Commune's fire clearance is refused, carry out the required fire-safety upgrades and request a re-inspection; ITM findings are cured through a corrective action plan filed with the labour inspector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale de l'industrie (Ministère de l'Économie, 19-21 boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg); not applicable to ISIC 6201 pure software and cloud services, which are liberal professions outside the Law of 2 September 2011 on business establishment authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) under the Law of 2 September 2011 — not required for the target ICT activity; the company operates solely upon RCS registration, the AEDT national number and ordinary municipal premises compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity, 1 Avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Class 4 tertiary/office activity under the amended Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 April 2009 on environmental impact assessment; no environmental operating permit or full EIA report is required for a software, cloud and financial portfolio tracking business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for server-based fintech operations; no industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources. If on-site IT equipment is deployed, comply with the WEEE regime of the Law of 24 April 2018 on electrical and electronic equipment waste, and with the convention on energy efficiency for office equipment; office waste handling per municipal waste regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (attestation de sécurité) from the Commune of the registered office after inspection by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) under the amended Law of 17 June 1994 on fire and rescue services, including verified escape routes, smoke detection and extinguisher coverage; structural load compliance confirmed through the Commune's building-permit file. Workplace clearance requires registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and compliance with the Law of 17 June 1994 on occupational safety and health, covering electrical safety, first-aid equipment, workstation ergonomics and, where applicable, a staff safety delegate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; official portals: guichet.lu, myguichet.lu, and impotsdirects.public.lu; RCSL (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) for business registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL or register a Luxembourg branch/PE with the RCSL through a notary or registered agent, thereby obtaining the 11-digit national identification number (matricule) which serves as the corporate TIN for direct tax purposes. Step 2 — File VAT registration with the AEDT (form 563) via myguichet.lu to obtain a VAT ID in the format 'LU' + 8 digits; provide constitutional documents, proof of economic activity, director identity documents, and a signed power of attorney. Step 3 — Non-EU applicants must appoint an AEDT-approved fiscal representative (représentant responsable solidaire) and may be required to post a bank guarantee; EU applicants may register directly. Step 4 — Mandatory electronic filing via the Luxembourg e-tax portal; processing generally completes within 1–2 weeks. Step 5 — Register with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) if any employees are hired.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; Luxembourg applies substance-over-form classification. Available elections include: (i) group taxation (intégration fiscale) effective for corporate income tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2025, allowing a dominant company to consolidate 95%-held Luxembourg subsidiaries with unanimous consent; (ii) participation exemption, automatic upon satisfaction of the 10% or EUR 6 million acquisition cost test, 12-month holding period, and subject to re-sale/substance conditions (exempts dividends and capital gains with no specific election but conditions must be evidenced); (iii) option for the 50% exemption on qualifying dividend income; (iv) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election for closely linked entities; (v) advance pricing agreements and upfront VAT confirmation requests with the ACD/AEDT. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 2 (Articles 168quinquies and 168sexies LIR) override any elective mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi du 12 février 1979)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for established taxable persons — every economic activity in Luxembourg triggers VAT registration from the first euro; domestic small-business exemption under Article 57 of the VAT Code applies to turnover up to EUR 30,000 (harmonised EU SME scheme per Directive 2020/285 applicable from 1 January 2025); intra-EU cross-border distance sales and B2C e-services benefit from the EUR 10,000 OSS/Union threshold before the place of supply shifts to the customer's member state.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general B2B real-time fiscal clearance, API digital reporting, or digital stamping regime applies in Luxembourg. Structured electronic invoicing (Peppol BIS/UBL) is mandatory only for B2G invoices in public procurement, in force since 2019. For B2B/B2C, the VAT Code requires sequential invoice numbering, customer VAT ID where applicable, complete service/goods description, and invoice issuance within one month of the supply. The EU ViDA package (mandatory e-invoicing and digital reporting for intra-EU supplies) is expected to apply from 1 January 2030 and is not yet implemented.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports are zero-rated under Article 54 of the VAT Code provided dispatch/transport outside the EU is completed within 3 months. For SaaS financial portfolio tracking services: (i) B2B services supplied to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place of supply at the customer's establishment per Article 14(4) VAT Code), effectively 0%; (ii) B2C e-services to non-EU consumers are outside the scope where the consumer's usual residence is outside the EU; (iii) intra-EU B2C e-services are taxed at the customer's local rate via the OSS scheme (Union scheme), with zero-rating available only for non-EU supplies; (iv) services ancillary to exported goods are zero-rated. Substantiation evidence includes contracts identifying the non-EU customer, customer local VAT/registration ID, IP/geolocation logs for B2C transactions, service delivery records, and routing of payment to a non-EU bank. Note: sales through Apple IAP may treat Apple as seller of record, w i t h VAT handled by Apple; the SARL must confirm contractual billing terms to determine its own VAT filing exposure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EAAD/IM-Export system) — required only for physical goods; for intangible SaaS services substitute the commercial contract, statements of work, and non-EU customer due diligence file
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill or verified service delivery log evidencing physical removal from the EU (goods) or remote service provisioning (SaaS)

Inward Remittance Certificate — not a Luxembourg statutory document; replace with bank/SWIFT/SEPA transfer evidence, payment gateway settlement records, and the AEDT-prescribed proof-of-payment register
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation obligation; the 180-day figure is a conservative internal treasury benchmark. Failure to substantiate zero-rating triggers retrospective VAT reassessment within the 5-year limitation period (10 years for fraud), monthly late-interest of 0.6%, and a 10% late-payment surcharge. Incorrect zero-rating claims cause clawback of input VAT credits plus administrative fines under Articles 55–59 of the VAT Code (range EUR 10–10,000, or 10%–100% of the evaded tax). Criminal tax fraud under Articles 61–65 is punishable with additional fines up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment; the principal and its Luxembourg fiscal representative are jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a Eurozone member, guarantees full current and capital account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU. No exchange control authorisation is required for profit remittance, dividend repatriation, repayment of shareholder loans, or liquidation proceeds. The SARL may freely hold and disburse EUR and foreign-currency accounts at Luxembourg banks. Dividends are generally subject to a 15% domestic withholding tax, which is eliminated or reduced under applicable tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, provided the participation exemption or holding requirements are met. Any restrictions arise exclusively from EU/UN targeted financial sanctions, CSSF AML/CFT enforcement, and FATF-related anti-money laundering screening, not from currency convertibility rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters and service providers may retain receipts in the original currency. Residents are only required to report cross-border flows and external positions to the BCL for balance-of-payments and international investment position statistics, in accordance with BCL reporting circulars and Regulation (EC) No 2157/1999 as implemented nationally. No minimum repatriation percentage applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) - Luxembourg
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) - Luxembourg

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions passported into Luxembourg under PSD2; Low for non-EEA offshore EMIs that lack a Luxembourg or EU passport. Any EMI-based treasury or clearing solution must hold e-money authorisation under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 2019 on payment and e-money services, or benefit from an EEA passport, and must comply with safeguarding duties, client-fund segregation, and AML/CFT rules supervised by the CSSF. Unlicensed offshore EMIs may not legally provide payment services to residents or establish collection mechanisms in Luxembourg. The SARL may nonetheless use a foreign EMI for yield or payment orchestration on a reverse-solicited basis only where the service is not marketed in Luxembourg and the LMSF risk review concludes that the foreign EMI's authorisation aligns with EU equivalence rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and a face-to-face interview are the default standard for onboarding directors, shareholders, and UBOs holding a 25% or greater interest in a newly formed SARL. A notarised constitutional dossier, Registry of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, identification documents, proof of residential address, and proof of a Luxembourg economic or registered office are mandatory. Remote video KYC may be accepted by certain tier-1 banks for low-risk corporate clients, but it is a discretionary derogation and is generally refused for non-resident, offshore, or substance-light structures. A direct interview of the legal representative and UBOs is required unless a bank expressly waives it in writing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO structure opacity involving bearer shares, trusts, or multi-tier third-country cascades
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE certificate (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), notarised corporate chart, organisational chart with economic ownership percentages, certified passports of all UBOs, 12-month source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements, statutory declaration confirming absence of bearer shares under the Law of 11 January 2019, and a CSSF-compliant AML risk classification memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening hit on an ultimate investor, counterparty, or foreign parent company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filtered sanctions and watch-list report (Refinitiv/World-Check or equivalent) showing no match or a clear rationale for a low residual risk, PEP risk assessment, proof of European/global context, evidence of Luxembourg economic substance (lease contract, payroll, social security filings, board minutes, local bank account), and a legal opinion from Luxembourg counsel establishing that no EU/UN targeted financial sanction applies to the proposed transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic substance or lack of business purpose for the SARL in a Fintech/software holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance file containing the Luxembourg lease agreement (commercial or office premises), monthly payroll records and social security declarations, minutes of board of managers meetings held in Luxembourg, copies of Luxembourg VAT registration, tax filings, and contracts demonstrating that strategic management decisions are made in Luxembourg, plus a detailed business plan showing the SARL's intended function as the host of the financial portfolio tracking application and treasury operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a LU_SARL inbound capital injection: (i) execute a SWIFT MT103 wire for USD/GBP or a SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) for EUR from the foreign parent/investor to the Luxembourg bank account of the SARL; (ii) include the full legal name 'LU_SARL', the IBAN, BIC of the receiving Luxembourg bank, and the reference 'Capital contribution - Shareholders Agreement dated [date]'; (iii) state an appropriate ISO 20022 external purpose code, e.g., 'EQUI' for equity contributions, 'LOAN' for shareholder advances, or 'COST' for paid-in capital and notarised company costs; (iv) annex to the transfer or provide to the bank the notarised capital contribution deed, the shareholders agreement, and UBO source-of-wealth documentation. No BCL exchange approval is required; the bank verifies identity, source of funds, and entire relevant sanctions exposure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements are cleared primarily via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated EU/EEA trade liabilities and via SWIFT MT103 for non-EU open-account trade disbursements. For physical-goods trade, a conforming commercial letter of credit may be issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank under UCP 600, but for software, SaaS subscriptions, and intellectual-property licensing, the standard rails are SWIFT MT103 with remittance information (field 70) and proper VAT invoicing. For consumer receipts from Stripe and Apple IAP, the SARL receives aggregated payouts through partner payment processors, which are then swept to the Luxembourg operational account via card-rail settlement or MT103 transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards traded OTC with CSSF-licensed banks under ISDA 2002 and EMIR clearing obligations
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on soft or restricted currencies with ISDA counterparties, subject to collateral and clearing rules where applicable
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for intercompany funding and asset-liability management
European-style FX options used exclusively for hedging, subject to the SARL's MiFID II classification and PRIIPs/KID documentation whenever offered by a Luxembourg bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (Financial Statements) deposit with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and no later than seven months after financial year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); electronic filing required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 50 to EUR 2,000 per director; repeated default may lead to civil summons and administrative strike-off of the SARL from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., by 31 December 2026 for FY 2025); extension may be granted on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; additional penalties for wilful omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same calendar deadline as corporate income tax return, typically 31 December of the following year; extension possible.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to 10% of assessed net wealth tax; monthly late interest at 0.8%; surcharges for incomplete filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) acting on behalf of the municipal commune of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as corporate income tax return; filed jointly with Form 100 where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed municipal tax; interest at 0.8% per month; enforcement by tax collector for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation filing (beneficial owners register confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), operated by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 15 March each year; updates within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership, with the annual confirmation cycle resetting thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 per infringement and additional EUR 250 per day of delay; criminal sanctions for wilful omissions or false declarations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for an SARL exceeding at least two of three criteria at balance-sheet date: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees 50. Audit is also compulsory for banks, insurance undertakings, UCITS/IFMs, securitisation vehicles and other supervised entities irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on registries and annual accounts, as amended (transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS-EU may be used in consolidated financial statements and, in limited cases, for parent entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All SARLs must file an annual confirmation of beneficial owner data with the RBE by 15 March. Any shareholding transfer or movement of indirect ownership must be filed with the RBE within 30 days; thereafter the company must update its internal register of members, preserve share transfer forms and approval minutes, and continue the annual confirmation cycle.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate Luxembourg City standard: 15% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains for shareholdings of ≥10% held for ≥12 months); IP regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income); notional interest deduction on new equity; investment tax credit up to 8%; loss carryforward indefinitely; 0% withholding tax on certain EU/ Treaty-protected dividend, interest, and royalty flows.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Fichier 564 (Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax return), filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / eTVA of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year); quarterly advance CIT/ municipal-business-tax prepayments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end the return is due by 31 May of the following year, with extension possible via written request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, RCS number, LEI, Luxembourg registered office, Luxembourg TIN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg registered office of the Sàrl and local tax ID; non-resident directors may be listed as authorised representatives without altering tax residence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account summary: gross revenue, operating expenses, depreciation, net profit/loss before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS figures reconciled to local statutory accounts; for a fully resident Sàrl include worldwide income, with foreign PE income exempt where a DTA applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: non-deductible expenses, tax-free capital gains, participation exemption claims, dividends received exemption, IP regime deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule evidencing holding period and ≥10% participation for dividend/ capital-gain exemption; provide similar documentation for IP regime eligibility

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments, including municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute from Box 3 after applicable deductions; non-resident shareholders' home-country relief does not affect Luxembourg base

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward and current-year loss declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is unlimited but losses may be forfeited on a >25% ownership/ business change; attach ownership continuity schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax certificates and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List Luxembourg dividend/interest/royalty WHT recovered or treaty claimed; non-resident claim of domestic WHT is generally not available absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions schedule: intercompany loans, licensing, management fees, IP sharing arrangements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose controlled foreign counterparties, transfer pricing method, arm's-length benchmarks, and any taxpayer's active role in EU non-cooperative jurisdiction lists

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing can trigger a default tax assessment, an administrative surcharge up to 10% of the tax due, late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, and, for persistent non-compliance, a civil fine up to EUR 250,000 plus criminal liability in cases of fraudulent concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (statutory withholding tax on Luxembourg dividends); reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or Luxembourg participation exemption where the recipient holds ≥10% for at least 12 months; DTA relief may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 15% depending on holding and residency
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty at source, the payee must provide the Luxembourg paying agent with a certificate of tax residence (Form 587 or approved form) and supporting ownership/beneficial ownership evidence before payment; if tax is withheld at the statutory 15%, a refund may be claimed within five years from the end of the calendar year of distribution by filing the prescribed ACD refund application and TRC with the Luxembourg tax office; EU-qualifying corporate parents may submit Form RED/1 or similar EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg statutory withholding tax on interest and royalties paid to a non-resident is generally 0%; the EU Interest & Royalty Directive and most Luxembourg DTAs also provide 0% withholding for qualifying associated enterprises; a 20% withholding tax applies only on interest or royalty payments made to entities resident in EU-list non-cooperative jurisdictions or low-tax jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 annual aggregate related-party transactions generally triggers the duty to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (local file/master file); financial-related-party transactions may reach the EUR 2,000,000 tier; CbC report required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not an ESR-jurisdiction with a standalone offshore economic substance regime, but tax-resident companies must present real substance (offices, full-time staff, actual decision-making in Luxembourg) to claim treaty and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits; the Luxembourg tax administration and courts apply substance-over-form, GAAR, and ATAD-inspired anti-abuse rules to deny benefits to shell and letterbox companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing a false Fichier 564 with understated subscription revenue, omitted Luxembourg bank accounts, or inflated costs in the portfolio-tracking Sàrl; deliberately destroying accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment plus monthly late-payment interest (0.8% per month), penalty of up to 10% of the understated tax for failure to declare, and, in criminal tax fraud cases, a fine up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years under Luxembourg tax and criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false returns are personally exposed to criminal fines, imprisonment, disqualification from Luxembourg board mandates for up to 10 years, and, if a flight risk is shown, a Schengen-area travel/exit ban; civil restitution and bankruptcy clawback may pierce the Sàrl veil when assets were diverted through the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Sàrl solely as a conduit to receive royalties or dividends from IP or portfolio assets and immediately route profits to a zero-tax parent, with no local employees, premises, or board activity; falsely claiming treaty/DTA benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and EU Directive benefits; ACD recharacterizes the structure, assesses the entire profit at 24.94% combined Luxembourg rate, imposes a 10% tax penalty, and may apply anti-abuse penalties of up to 25% of the additional tax; the company may be struck off or wound up for non-genuine activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil liability for dividends paid out of artificially created profits if the corporate veil is pierced; criminal prosecution for forgery and tax fraud where the shell routing was knowingly executed can lead to imprisonment, fines, and an exit/travel ban in pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering personal wealth analytics and portfolio-tracking software that facilitates crypto-asset transfers, cross-border money movement, or anonymous investment tracking without registration or licensing with the CSSF where AML obligations apply; using low-risk app revenue labels to launder third-party proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended), administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; criminal money laundering penalties up to 5 years’ imprisonment and fines up to EUR 1,250,000; confiscation of laundered property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly deploy the platform to launder funds are criminally liable; assets may be frozen, European Arrest Warrants may be issued for cross-border flight, directors face imprisonment and travel bans, and the Sàrl’s limited liability will not shield intentional criminal acts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious or non-arm's-length management fees, unrealistically low intra-group interest rates, or backdated IP licensing contracts to shift profits; claiming enhanced notional interest deduction without substantive equity structure or lender substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment by the Luxembourg tax authorities plus secondary adjustment (reclassifying excess deductions as hidden dividends), late-payment interest of 0.8% per month and a 10%–25% transfer pricing penalty; repeated deceptive documentation can be prosecuted as tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute or approve sham transfer pricing contracts are jointly and severally liable for tax deficiencies arising from deliberately fraudulent acts; criminal conviction may include imprisonment, personal fines, disqualification from corporate office, and a travel ban pending investigation.
